findings.title: The idea fits in one sentence
findings.evidence: T-ONE-SENTENCE fails. The eyebrow 'AI-NATIVE WORKFLOWS', the h1 'Build faster with intelligent workflows for modern teams' and the sub-line 'The all-in-one platform that helps product teams ship better software in record time. findings.title: Software shows its own UI at work

findings.before: Peach glow and grid lines as the lead picture
findings.after: Lead with the product at work: one real workflow in the Lumina interface on the first screen [DATA NEEDED: product screenshot]

findings.where: whole page, 1440 and 375, tiles/1440-00.png to tiles/1440-02.png
findings.evidence: The palette table gives the page ground #faf6ef, the ink #1f1a15, the body grey #5b4f44 and one chromatic group, terracotta #c8552b (6 uses). The sweep's look_family hit matches warm-paper-serif on 6 of 6 tells (cream_bg #faf6ef, terracotta_accent #c8552b, Fraunces display, italic serif hero). The only brand mark is a 10px terracotta dot before the "Lumina" wordmark, and the customer names are set as plain italic text, so no logo, product shot or photograph supplies the colours.
findings.before: Cream, brown-black and terracotta taken as a set from the warm-paper look
findings.after: An accent and paper sampled from the product's own mark or screenshots (Sample, Converge, Justify), with the cream kept only if the brand chose it
findings.why: The palette identifies the page as one more warm-paper template, so it cannot help a visitor remember this product.
findings.fix: Use the brand's colours. With none, sample from the client's photographs or product, converge to a few, and write the one-sentence reason next to the tokens.

findings.title: Display type is set in ink
findings.evidence: The palette table records one display-text use of #c8552b at 1440: the italic word "intelligent" inside the 80px h1 "Build faster with intelligent workflows for modern teams".

findings.after: The whole h1 in the ink #1f1a15; emphasis, if any, from the italic alone
findings.why: The largest coloured mark on the screen is a word in a headline, not the "Start free trial" action, which is ink.
findings.fix: Set display type in ink and keep the accent for the action under it.

findings.title: The accent marks action and state
findings.where: eyebrow and section numbers, 1440, tiles/1440-00.png, tiles/1440-01.png, tiles/1440-02.png
findings.evidence: Terracotta (#c8552b and the darker #a8431f) colours the eyebrow "AI-NATIVE WORKFLOWS", the section numbers "01", "02" and "03" and the logo dot. All four buttons ("Get started", "Start free trial", "Watch demo", "Start your free trial") are ink or paper. The sweep's A11-001 hit on "03" (#a8431f on #1f1a15, 2.87:1 at 375) is the same label colour.
findings.before: The accent on labels and numbers only; no action uses it
findings.after: Labels and numbers in the muted grey #5b4f44; the accent, if kept, given to the primary action
findings.why: The accent decorates labels while the actions get none, so colour tells the visitor nothing about what to press.
findings.fix: Remove the accent from decoration and labels; keep it on the action and the current state.

findings.title: The palette converges to a few roles
findings.evidence: The three feature cards use full-colour emoji as icons: an orange lightning bolt, a yellow padlock and a blue-and-purple chart. The blue and purple appear nowhere else on the page, and the palette table measures 0% chromatic area elsewhere besides the terracotta.
findings.before: Emoji icons that bring yellow, blue and purple into a one-accent palette
findings.after: Icons drawn in the ink or the muted grey, so the palette keeps one accent
findings.why: The emoji add three hues with no role and make the cards read as placeholders.
findings.fix: List each colour's role, merge near neighbours, and drop or demote the second accent.

findings.title: Adjective claims where a mechanism belongs
findings.evidence: Failed T-THREE-LINE on all three cards: 'Lightning Fast: Move from idea to production in minutes, not months. Our AI handles the heavy lifting so you can focus on what matters.', 'Your data is safe, always.' and 'Lumina grows with your team without breaking a sweat.' None can be pictured or proven false. 'SOC 2 compliant infrastructure with end-to-end encryption' is the only checkable claim, and it is category stock. 'Trusted by 10,000+' is the sweep's invented_metrics hit.
findings.before: Our AI handles the heavy lifting so you can focus on what matters.
findings.after: Say which step the AI does (for example, which part of the workflow it writes or routes) and show one real example.
findings.why: Adjective claims give the reader nothing to test or remember.
findings.fix: Name how it works or what it measures ('syncs every 30 seconds', 'Revenue grew 34% to $12M'), using supplied facts only; otherwise cut the claim or leave a [DATA NEEDED] slot.

findings.title: Cadence devices in every block
findings.evidence: Failed T-CADENCE: the copy sheet counts a contrast frame ('in minutes, not months'); the features intro is a fragment triad ('One platform. Endless possibilities. Built for teams who care about craft.'); the sub-line ends on a chiasmus pair ('Powered by AI, designed for humans.'); two cards end on a quip ('Your data is safe, always.', 'without breaking a sweat'). That is a device in every block of a 166-word page.
findings.before: One platform. Endless possibilities. Built for teams who care about craft.
findings.after: Cut the intro line; let the cards carry specific facts.
findings.why: The repeated rhythm reads as the model's default register, not a brand voice.
findings.fix: Keep the strongest instance of each device and rewrite the rest as plain statements that end on information.

findings.title: Model-default voice
findings.evidence: Failed T-READ-ALOUD: the footer line '© 2025 Lumina, Inc. — Crafted with care in San Francisco.', 'Built for teams who care about craft' and 'designed for humans' are the warm, modest self-description that fits nine of nine SaaS sites; no brand voice is supplied in the run.
findings.before: Crafted with care in San Francisco.
findings.after: Cut the self-description; if the place matters, state the fact plainly.
findings.why: A business calling itself careful is a claim the reader cannot check.
findings.fix: Write a short voice card from the brief (register, three traits, words the client uses and avoids), then rewrite the hero and headings in it. Run the nine-trades test: the voice should fit none of nine other businesses.

findings.title: One action under several labels
findings.evidence: Failed T-LABEL-READ: the sign-up action reads 'Get started' (nav), 'Start free trial →' (hero) and 'Start your free trial →' (closing), so the closing action is worded differently from the hero's. The sweep covers the glued arrows.
findings.before: Get started / Start free trial / Start your free trial
findings.after: Use 'Start free trial' in all three places.
findings.why: Three wordings for one action ask the reader to check whether they differ.
findings.fix: Name the action and its object; pick one wording for the main action and use it at every placement.

findings.evidence: The page is five sections in stock order: a centred hero with eyebrow "01 AI-NATIVE WORKFLOWS", a row of six italic wordmarks (Northwind, Halcyon, Meridian, Fieldnote, Atlas & Co., Verity), three icon cards ("Lightning Fast", "Enterprise Secure", "Built to Scale"), a dark CTA band ("Ready to transform how your team builds?") and a one-line footer. The sections are numbered 01, 02, 03 as if the order were an argument.
findings.before: Hero, logos, three feature cards, CTA band, footer.
findings.after: Replace the feature cards with one section that shows a workflow being run in the product, and put it directly under the hero. [DATA NEEDED: a real product screen or workflow example]
findings.why: Every section would sit unchanged under another product's name, so the visitor cannot tell what Lumina does after reading the whole page.
findings.title: Section order follows the argument
findings.fix: Move the strongest real section to second place; cut stock sections that have no material.

findings.evidence: The image list holds no product screenshot, demo or example; the only visuals are a grid background, three emoji-style icons and text wordmarks. The job is trying a workflow tool, and the page offers "Watch demo" without showing anything of it.
findings.before: A trial page with no view of the product.
findings.after: Add the category's own section: the product's main screen or a short workflow walk-through beside the hero. [DATA NEEDED: product screenshots]
findings.why: Visitors to a software trial page decide on what the product looks like in use; without it, the trial button asks for trust the page has not earned.
findings.title: Anatomy fits the visitor's job
findings.fix: Move the job's action into the nav and hero, and add the missing job section the client has material for; [DATA NEEDED: what] where they do not.

findings.evidence: In dom-375.json the "Start free trial" link sits at y=834 with h=77, so its bottom edge is at 911px, below the 812px fold. The h1 wraps to five lines at 48px and the subhead to five more before the button.
findings.before: Primary action below the first phone screen.
findings.after: Shorten the h1 or reduce its phone size so the action sits inside the first 812px.
findings.why: On a phone the first screen holds only an eyebrow, a headline and a paragraph; the visitor must scroll to reach the one action the page exists for.
findings.title: The first screen answers what, for whom and what next
findings.fix: Shorten or shrink what pushes the action down (an oversized visual, a second paragraph), never the action itself.

findings.evidence: All three h1 and h2 elements are text-align center, and the three feature cards centre their icon, h3 and body text too. The hero stacks the number, the eyebrow, the h1, the subhead, both buttons and the trust line on one centred axis.
findings.before: Every block on the centre axis.
findings.after: Set the feature section and its cards on a left edge, and keep centring only for the hero if at all.
findings.why: With everything on one centred axis there is no edge for the eye to follow, and the centred card text has ragged starts on both sides.
findings.title: One alignment axis
findings.fix: Left-align the heading groups and body; keep centring for one short display line.

findings.title: Saturated faces need an argument
findings.where: every heading and the logo row, 1440 and 375 (tiles/1440-00.png, 1440-01.png)
findings.evidence: fonts.json at 1440 shows Fraunces drawing the h1 (88px), both h2s (52 and 60px), the h3 card titles (22px), the wordmark "Lumina" and the italic fake customer logos ("Northwind", "Halcyon", "Meridian"). Inter draws everything else. data/lexicons/fonts.yaml lists Fraunces as saturated, and the sweep's look_family detector matches the warm-paper-serif cluster on 6 of 6 tells (cream page, terracotta accent, serif display, italic serif hero, eyebrows, numbered labels). No contract or brand names either face.
findings.before: Fraunces display and italic logos over Inter body, with no stated source
findings.after: A display face chosen for the brief (see substitutes in data/lexicons/fonts.yaml), or a recorded reason for Fraunces in the contract
findings.why: Fraunces with Inter on cream is the current generator default for a warm SaaS page, so the type tells the reader nothing about Lumina.
findings.root: the display and body font tokens
findings.fix: Keep the face if the brand chose it; otherwise try a same-build substitute from data/lexicons/fonts.yaml.

findings.title: Headings are set in one voice
findings.evidence: The type table lists one heading child set apart in style and colour: "intelligent" in the h1 "Build faster with intelligent workflows for modern teams" is italic Fraunces in terracotta at 88px (1440) and 48px (375). The sweep's look_family detector records the same as its italic_serif_hero tell.
findings.before: "Build faster with *intelligent* workflows" with the adjective in italic terracotta
findings.after: The h1 in one style and one colour
findings.why: An italic accent on the vaguest word in the headline is the generator's signature move, and it puts the stress on a word that says nothing specific.
findings.fix: Set the heading in one weight, one style and one colour; move the stress to a line break.

findings.title: Prose has a readable measure
findings.where: div.card > p in the features grid, 375 (tiles/375-02.png)
findings.evidence: At 375 the type table finds three card paragraphs below 16 characters a line: "Move from idea to production in minutes..." runs 10 lines at 12 characters (99px wide), "SOC 2 compliant infrastructure..." 8 lines at 11 (108px), and "From your first prototype to millions of users..." 14 lines at 7 (69px). The page overflows to about 698px wide at 375 (tiles/375-00.png), so the grid keeps three columns.
findings.before: Three card columns at 375, 69 to 108px wide
findings.after: One card column below about 640px, so card text runs about 35 to 45 characters a line
findings.why: Seven to twelve characters a line breaks almost every phrase, and the reader re-scans the next line every two words.
findings.root: the features grid with no single-column breakpoint
findings.fix: Set max-width in ch on the paragraph, not on the wrapper.

findings.title: Headlines fit their length
findings.evidence: The 55-character h1 sets at 48px over 5 lines of text at 375 ("Build faster / with / intelligent / workflows for / modern teams"), with "with" alone on a line, plus a caret bar below. At 1440 it runs 3 lines at 88px. The sweep's widows hit records a 1% last line at 1280.

findings.after: A 36 to 40px h1 at 375 so it holds to 3 lines
findings.why: At phone width the headline takes the whole first screen and breaks "with" out on its own.
findings.fix: Shorten the line or step the size down; move the detail into the line under it.

findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 Non-text Content: decorative symbols should be hidden from assistive tech.
findings.title: Keep all words as real text in reading order

findings.evidence: Read in order, the headings are "Build faster with intelligent workflows for modern teams", "Everything you need to ship great products", "Ready to transform how your team builds?". The h3s are "Lightning Fast", "Enterprise Secure", "Built to Scale".
findings.before: Headings that name categories and promises only.
findings.after: Write each head as a specific claim about what the workflow does. [DATA NEEDED: the product's actual workflows]
findings.why: The heading outline says 'a faster platform' and nothing else; a scanning visitor learns no fact.
findings.title: Headings and hero tell the story
findings.fix: Rewrite each category heading as the section's claim, in the section's own nouns.

findings.title: Lines break where the sense breaks
findings.evidence: The type table lists four controls that wrap to 2 lines at 375: "Sign in" (14px), "Get started" (14px), "Start free trial →" (15px, the arrow drops to its own line) and "Watch demo" (15px).
findings.before: "Sign / in", "Start free trial / →"
findings.after: white-space: nowrap on nav links and buttons, with the nav collapsing to a menu at 375
findings.why: A wrapped button label reads as two items, and the arrow alone on a line looks like a separate control.
findings.fix: Add text-wrap: balance to heading roles, move or remove the manual break, and shorten the label rather than let it wrap.
